guardrail: Research is hypothesis generation only. No item in this file is allowed to change live predictions until separately validated.
research_summary: Evidence supports conditional short-horizon continuation, but exhaustion and reversal depend strongly on volatility regime, liquidity, volume, time of day, and catalyst context. The most promising tests separate impulse quality from pullback quality, model repeated-bounce decay, and enforce chronological discovery and validation for unknown motifs.

hypotheses.title: Impulse quality predicts pullback continuation
hypotheses.claim: After a catalyst-driven impulse, a shallow pullback with declining relative volume and stable VWAP distance is more likely to produce a higher high than a deep, high-volume pullback.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Separates orderly absorption from distribution and may distinguish quick bounces from genuine continuation.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability of making a new session high within 5, 15, and 30 minutes after pullback completion.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Continuation probability rises with shallow retracement, volume contraction, VWAP support, and improving liquidity.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Event study with causal timestamps, purged walk-forward validation, and net-of-spread outcome labels.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Positive out-of-sample calibration improvement versus impulse-return and time-of-day baselines across at least three market regimes and multiple calendar years.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: No stable out-of-sample lift, effect disappears after spread/slippage costs, or performance is concentrated in one ticker or catalyst class.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Repeated-bounce decay and late-bounce failure
hypotheses.claim: The second and third bounces from a local support level have smaller median gains and higher failure risk than the first bounce, especially when each bounce forms a lower high or occurs on declining volume.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Directly tests a common but insufficiently quantified exhaustion concept and can define failure severity.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward maximum favorable and adverse excursion, probability of a 5% or 10% fall from bounce high, and minutes to failure.
conditioning_variables: Borrow or short-sale constraints when available
hypotheses.expected_direction: Later bounces show declining upside, shorter duration, and greater probability of rapid failure; lower highs amplify the effect.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Define support algorithmically, stratify by bounce number, and estimate survival curves and competing-risk outcomes using only information available at each bounce.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Monotonic deterioration in at least two independent forward metrics with confidence intervals excluding zero in chronological holdouts.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Bounce count adds no information beyond volatility, retracement, and time-of-day controls, or 5%/10% risks are unstable across price and liquidity buckets.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Failed reclaim and failed breakout as exhaustion signals
hypotheses.claim: A failed VWAP, prior-high, or range-breakout reclaim followed by renewed selling predicts larger short-horizon drawdowns than a simple pullback that remains above the reclaimed level.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Failed reclaims encode trapped breakout buyers and may identify exhaustion earlier than raw price weakness.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability of a 3%, 5%, and 10% decline from failure price within 15, 30, and 120 minutes.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Fast rejection, high failure volume, spread widening, and lower highs predict larger and faster drawdowns.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Use matched event studies against non-failed pullbacks, with ticker-day clustered errors and execution-aware midpoint or conservative fill assumptions.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Stable incremental predictive value over VWAP distance, recent return, realized volatility, and volume percentile in unseen ticker-days.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Signal vanishes after controlling for contemporaneous order imbalance or is driven by a small number of halted or illiquid names.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Liquidity-adjusted momentum and volume climax
hypotheses.claim: Impulse continuation is strongest when abnormal volume expands without disproportionate spread widening; volume climax accompanied by deteriorating depth and widening spreads predicts exhaustion instead.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Raw volume is ambiguous: it can represent informed participation, forced trading, or temporary liquidity withdrawal.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward return, maximum excursion, and probability of reversal below impulse midpoint over 5 to 60 minutes.
hypotheses.expected_direction: High volume with stable or improving liquidity supports continuation; high volume with spread/depth deterioration predicts exhaustion.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Panel regression and nonlinear tree models with cross-sectional normalization by ticker and time bucket; report results by liquidity decile.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Effect remains economically positive after conservative transaction costs and survives removal of the least liquid 10% of observations.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Volume features add no value after dollar-turnover, spread, and volatility controls, or results depend on one feed's quote artifacts.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Step-plateau-reacceleration regime
hypotheses.claim: A multi-session advance followed by a higher-price plateau has elevated probability of reacceleration when the plateau shows reduced realized volatility, persistent higher lows, and renewed volume or catalyst intensity.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: Tests whether price acceptance at a higher level differs from a failed first impulse and captures multi-session continuation structures.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Probability of a new 20-day high or 5% advance within the next 1 to 5 sessions.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Narrowing ranges, higher lows, persistent closing strength, and renewed volume predict reacceleration; widening ranges and declining closes predict failure.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Construct features only from completed sessions, use expanding-window estimation and purged ticker-level validation, and compare against momentum, volatility, and gap baselines.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: Positive out-of-sample lift across at least four chronological test periods and at least two catalyst categories.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Pattern is not robust to alternative plateau definitions, corporate-action adjustments, or removal of extreme winners.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

hypotheses.title: Leakage-safe unnamed motif discovery
hypotheses.claim: Unsupervised motifs or regime transitions in normalized intraday price-volume-order-flow sequences can identify recurring states with stable forward outcomes without starting from a named setup.
hypotheses.why_it_might_matter: May discover useful impulse, exhaustion, or consolidation structures that handcrafted rules omit.
hypotheses.target_outcome: Forward return distribution, new-high probability, 5%/10% drawdown probability, and time-to-failure for each discovered motif.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Some clusters or change-point states should exhibit materially different continuation and failure distributions, but direction must be learned rather than assumed.
hypotheses.recommended_test: Discover motifs or clusters only on an earlier calendar block; freeze representations and labels; validate on later unseen dates using nested walk-forward splits, purging, embargoes, and multiple-testing correction.
hypotheses.minimum_evidence_to_promote: A motif remains distinct in later periods, has economically meaningful effect after costs, and beats matched handcrafted baselines in at least two independent holdouts.
hypotheses.failure_or_rejection_criteria: Cluster membership is unstable, outcomes regress toward the unconditional mean, discovery and validation periods overlap, or performance disappears under alternate sampling and normalization choices.
hypotheses.promotion_gate: Must be implemented as a leakage-safe historical experiment and pass out-of-sample / walk-forward validation before use.

important_caveats: Intraday effects can be dominated by the U-shaped volume and volatility cycle; all tests need time-of-day normalization.
Low-priced and low-float stocks have large spreads, price impact, halts, and data-quality risks; midpoint returns can materially overstate executable results.
Catalyst labels, float, shares outstanding, borrow data, and historical news timestamps require point-in-time reconstruction.
Avoid random row-wise splits; use chronological splits, ticker-day grouping, purging, embargoes, and frozen feature transformations.
Control for multiple hypotheses, repeated experimentation, survivorship, delistings, corporate actions, halts, and venue coverage.
A statistically significant continuation effect is not necessarily tradable after spread, slippage, latency, partial fills, and market-impact costs.
research_gaps: How do second- and third-bounce failure hazards vary by catalyst credibility and news recency?
Can quote-level depth and signed trade data distinguish absorption from hidden distribution reliably?
Which motif representations remain stable across tick-size, venue, and market-regime changes?
What are the best point-in-time definitions of float turnover for rapidly changing share counts?
How should halt risk and reopening gaps be incorporated into forward excursion and time-to-failure labels?
